strategy.thesis: Research-driven venture fund turning science fiction into scientific fact; backs outlier founders at the frontier of space and intelligence. Described as the only Taiwan-rooted VC dedicated exclusively to the space industry, having mapped 53 distinct space sub-sectors including lunar mining and space-based pharmaceuticals.

summary.en: Research-driven frontier-tech VC, originally launched as an MIT research group in 2016 and rooted in Taiwan, that has become the only Taiwan-linked fund dedicated exclusively to the space industry. Founder Poseidon Ho frames 2026 as 'the first year of the commercial space era'; portfolio includes Vast Space, Impulse Space and AstroForge.
summary.local: 由侯海琦（Poseidon Ho）創立、源自 MIT 研究小組、根植台灣的前沿科技創投，是台灣唯一專注太空產業的創投基金，投資組合涵蓋 Vast Space、Impulse Space、AstroForge 等。

sources.title: How a Taiwanese VC Broke Into the Commercial Space Industry

strategy.thesis: US-Taiwan space-tech bridge. Invests ~30-40% of Ignition Fund 1 in Taiwan space startups and the remainder in US companies required to partner with Taiwan's supply chain. Runs the Infinio Space Venture Studio (ISVS) using an 'investment brings orders' model pairing 10 international space firms with 10 Taiwanese supply-chain companies. Tagline: 'Democratizing Space.'

summary.en: Los Angeles-based space-tech VC that landed in Taiwan in July 2022, launching the US$20M Ignition Fund 1 to build a Taiwan space ecosystem. Pairs international space startups with Taiwanese supply-chain manufacturers through its Infinio Space Venture Studio (ISVS) 'investment brings orders' model. Alpha Networks (明泰科技) was its first institutional Taiwan investor.
summary.local: 總部位於洛杉磯的太空科技創投，2022 年 7 月來台啟動 2,000 萬美元的 Ignition Fund 1，以「投資帶訂單」的 ISVS 創投工作室模式串接國際太空新創與台灣供應鏈，明泰科技為首位台灣機構投資人。

A follow-on investor in TronFuture's NT$900M defense/satellite Series A, giving it niche exposure to Taiwan's space-defense dual-use sector.

strategy.thesis: Government-sponsored international accelerator landing program for space-tech startups: attracts international space startups to Taiwan, helps Taiwan-based space startups reach global markets, and bridges enterprises with startups for supply-chain partnerships in satellite manufacturing, launch components, and space-based applications.

program.eligibility: Company established less than 10 years; space-tech focus (satellite manufacturing/system integration, sensing/imaging, rocket components, space IoT)

track_record.portfolio_count: 16 teams (2023 inaugural cohort); ~10-11 teams from 7 countries (2024)

application.how_to_apply: Apply online via TAcc+ International Program page

summary.en: Taiwan government space-tech accelerator program run under TAcc+ by the SME and Startup Administration (MOEA) and executed by ITRI. Launched 2023 (16 inaugural international teams); pairs international space startups from Europe, India and Japan with Taiwan's satellite/semiconductor supply chain. The 2023 cohort generated six MOUs and 300+ supplier discussions.
summary.local: 經濟部中小及新創企業署主辦、工研院執行的 TAcc+ 國際太空科技新創支持計畫，2023 年啟動（首屆 16 隊），引進歐洲、印度、日本太空新創與台灣衛星半導體供應鏈媒合，2023 年促成 6 件 MOU 與逾 300 場供應商洽談。

strategy.thesis: First space-industry accelerator run by Taiwan's national space agency (TASA). Combines technical verification (TASA R&D and test resources), market export focus (VC introductions and international linkage to Silicon Valley/NASDAQ, Europe, Japan, UK), and Taiwan's semiconductor/ICT/manufacturing advantages, aiming to cultivate Taiwan's first space-industry unicorn.

investment.raw: Non-dilutive funding (modeled on NASA SBIR Ignite)

program.location: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University Po'ai Campus, Hsinchu
program.eligibility: Space-sector startups across satellite manufacturing supply chains, ground equipment/system integration, and data/AI services

application.how_to_apply: Via TASA (in recruitment phase ahead of Q3 2026 launch)

summary.en: Taiwan's first space-industry accelerator, established by the national space agency TASA, with launch expected Q3 2026 at NYCU's Po'ai Campus in Hsinchu. Offers non-dilutive funding modeled on NASA's SBIR Ignite, office space, technical mentorship and VC/international introductions; targets satellite manufacturing, ground systems and space data/AI, with the stated goal of producing Taiwan's first space unicorn.
summary.local: 國家太空中心（TASA）設立的台灣首座太空產業加速器，預計 2026 年第三季於陽明交大博愛校區啟用，提供仿效 NASA SBIR Ignite 的非稀釋性資金、場域、技術輔導與創投/國際媒合，鎖定衛星製造、地面系統與太空資料／AI，目標培育台灣首隻太空獨角獸。

name.local: 佳世達科技股份有限公司

strategy.thesis: Strategic corporate investor ('AI 大艦隊' / AI fleet) expanding into low-earth-orbit satellite and drone hardware. Takes minority stakes in dual-use space and unmanned-systems startups to integrate them into its manufacturing fleet and capture LEO satellite supply-chain and drone opportunities.

summary.en: Taiwanese ODM giant Qisda acts as a strategic corporate investor building an 'AI fleet,' investing NT$320M in LEO-satellite startup Rayonic (15.79% stake) in 2023 and adding drone makers Chyrung Tech and Xiang Long Aerospace. Gives it niche exposure across satellite and dual-use unmanned-systems supply chains.
summary.local: 佳世達以「AI 大艦隊」策略進行企業投資，2023 年以 3.2 億元投資低軌衛星新創鐳洋科技（持股 15.79%），並納入無人機廠擎壤科技與翔隆航太，布局衛星與無人載具雙用供應鏈。

strategy.thesis: Strategic corporate investor in millimeter-wave / phased-array RF for 5G, LEO satellite, HAPS and defense dual-use applications. Led TMYTEK's NT$100M A+ round (2020), holds the second-largest stake with a board seat, providing manufacturing/design resources for mmWave module mass production.

summary.en: Taiwanese ODM Inventec acts as a strategic corporate investor in deep-tech RF, leading TMYTEK's ~NT$100M A+ round in 2020 and holding the second-largest stake with a board seat. TMYTEK's millimeter-wave phased-array antennas serve 5G, LEO satellite, HAPS and defense dual-use markets, giving Inventec niche space-defense supply-chain exposure.
